summary: Dalnerechensk Airport (DLR) is a small regional airfield serving the town of Dalnerechensk in Primorsky Krai, in the Russian Far East. Located near the Bolshaya Ussurka River, it primarily supports general aviation and limited regional flights in this sparsely populated area near the Chinese border. The airport's modest infrastructure reflects its role as a local transport hub rather than a commercial gateway.
faqs:
Q: Does Dalnerechensk Airport handle commercial passenger flights?
A: Scheduled commercial passenger service is very limited or unavailable; the airport mainly accommodates general aviation and charter operations.

Q: Where is the airport located relative to the town?
A: It is situated on the outskirts of Dalnerechensk, within short driving distance of the town center.

Q: What facilities are available at DLR?
A: As a small airfield, it offers basic infrastructure with limited passenger amenities and no major terminal services.

Q: Are there alternative airports nearby?
A: Larger airports in the region include Vladivostok Knevichi (VVO) and Khabarovsk Novy (KHV), both several hundred kilometers away.
transport_tips: Ground transport to and from the airport is best arranged in advance, as public transit options are limited in this remote area. Taxis and private vehicles are the most common ways to reach the airfield from Dalnerechensk town center. Travelers should confirm transport availability before arrival, especially during winter months when conditions can be challenging.
local_tip: Pack warm layers even in shoulder seasons—Dalnerechensk experiences harsh continental winters with temperatures frequently dropping well below freezing due to its inland Far Eastern location.
